description: Sabotages for io-buffers. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: RegisteredSpan is three public fields and has no logic to sabotage. The traits' obligations -- an address that does not change while the kernel holds the value -- cannot be observed from a test that returns before any kernel would use the address, so what these entries pin is that each implementation reports the allocation it owns and the length it holds, which is what the obligation rests on. The aligned buffer's allocator-failure arm is reached by asking for the largest length that fits an isize, which no machine can provide; a failure of a request that ordinarily succeeds is not reachable on demand.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a Vec reports no address
sabotages.why: A null address is the one the kernel would be handed. Compared against the Vec's own pointer, not against another call to the same function, which a constant would satisfy.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a Vec reports its capacity as its length
sabotages.why: Bytes past the length are not initialized; an operation told it may use them reads or writes memory the owner never filled.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a Vec's mutable address is not its shared one
sabotages.why: The mutable trait's obligation is that its address equals the shared one, so the kernel writes where the owner reads.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a boxed slice reports no address
sabotages.why: As for a Vec.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a boxed slice reports half its length
sabotages.why: A short length is the safe direction, and still a wrong answer: an operation would transfer fewer bytes than the owner handed over.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a boxed slice's mutable address is not its shared one
sabotages.why: As for a Vec.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a shared slice reports no address
sabotages.why: The case the ring crate's mutation testing found: comparing the function to itself passes even when it returns null, so the test names the allocation independently.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a shared slice reports no length
sabotages.why: A zero length makes every operation over it a no-op that reports success.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a static slice reports no address
sabotages.why: As for a Vec.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a static mutable slice reports no mutable address
sabotages.why: The one reference type that is a legal destination: its mutable address must be the slice's.

sabotages.name: IB-1.1: a static mutable slice reports its length plus one
sabotages.why: A length past the allocation is the direction that lets the kernel write out of bounds.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: an alignment that is not a power of two is not refused
sabotages.why: Without the check the layout call refuses it for the wrong reason, and the caller is told its length was too large when its alignment was wrong.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: the layout ignores the alignment asked for
sabotages.why: The one promise the buffer exists to make. Every alignment test reads the address back.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: a layout that cannot be made is reported as a bad alignment
sabotages.why: The two reasons a layout fails are different faults of the caller's; the error names which.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: a failed allocation is reported as too large
sabotages.why: A caller sizing from a device's geometry shrinks on one and gives up on the other.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: the memory is not zeroed
sabotages.why: The buffer promises initialised bytes, which the traits require. Caught by allocating, dirtying and freeing a block and asking for the same size again; an allocator that happened to hand back zeroes would hide it, which is why the test repeats.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: from_bytes does not copy
sabotages.why: A buffer reported as holding the bytes it was given, and holding zeroes.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: a copy loses the alignment
sabotages.why: A copy of a sector-aligned buffer that is not sector-aligned fails an unbuffered write for a reason far from the copy.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: the reported alignment is one
sabotages.why: A caller checking the alignment before handing the buffer to a target is told it is unaligned.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: dropping a buffer does not free it
sabotages.why: A leak is invisible to every assertion but one that counts the allocator's live bytes, which these tests do.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: an empty buffer is freed too
sabotages.why: An empty buffer's address is dangling, never allocated; freeing it is undefined behaviour. Likely scored as a process abort from the allocator, which is a weaker catch than an assertion; the counting test's arithmetic also disagrees.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: equality ignores the alignment
sabotages.why: Alignment is part of what a buffer promises, so two buffers that differ in it are not equal.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: the trait reports the alignment as the length
sabotages.why: A kernel told it may use as many bytes as the alignment, not as many as the buffer holds.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: the mutable address is null
sabotages.why: The mutable trait's address must be the shared one. May be scored as a process abort by the tests that read through it; the correspondence test fails an assertion on its own.

sabotages.name: IB-1.4: Debug prints the contents
sabotages.why: An I/O buffer holds someone's data, and a Debug that printed it would put it in any log that formats the value.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: an empty buffer's address is made from the alignment at least one
sabotages.why: Equivalent: an alignment is never zero, so taking the larger of it and one changes nothing. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to text rather than behaviour.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: a Vec's address is read through its type rather than its method
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself: Vec::as_ptr(self) is the same call spelled differently, on code every Vec test runs. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to text rather than behaviour.
